description: The ocean biogeochemical model is based on COBALTv3 (Stock et al., 2025) with additional capabilities for COBALTv3.1 (Luo et al., in preparation). New modeled processes include a representation of anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox), the neritic burial of CaCO3 in shallow regions (O’Mara and Dunne 2019), enhanced respiration-driven CaCO3 remineralization associated with sinking organic matter detritus (Kwon et al. 2024), and fast-sinking nitrogen and phosphorus detritus (sinking speed of 600 m/d) from fishes (Luo et al. 2024). With the two additional detritus tracers, the total tracer count in COBALTv3.1 is 40.  Parameter modifications in COBALTv3.1 (relative to COBALTv3) include an adjustment of the dynamic N:P scheme based on Galbraith and Martiny (2015), to prevent high phosphate biases in the subtropics. The nitrification scheme was modified following a recent data compilation (Tang et al. 2023), field-based environmental manipulation experiments, and a random forest machine learning approach (Zhao et al. submitted). The iron scavenging rate was increased, while the half-saturation constant for phytoplankton iron uptake was decreased.  Another notable change are the river forcings to the ocean biogeochemical model. We adopt the convention from Dean et al. (2025) of distinguishing between “contemporary” DOC from recent plant productivity and associated soil microbial origin are delivered via rivers and are instantaneously remineralized at river mouths as DIC from riverine DIC and alkalinity inputs of “geologic” origin, which are associated with long-lived reservoirs and passed as weathered material into the coastal ocean as concentrations following Da et al. (2025). Riverine DIC from Da et al. (2025) was modified down to distinguish the geologic vs. contemporary sources.   Da, F., Stock, C. A., Dunne, J. P., Liu, X., Luo, J.
